Certus quartz buds will sprout from $(l:items_blocks_machines/budding_certus)budding certus blocks$(/l), similar to amethyst. If you

break a bud that is not finished growing, it will drop one $(l:items_blocks_machines/certus_quartz_dust)Certus Quartz Dust$(/l), unchanged by fortune. If you break a fully grown cluster, it will drop four $(l:items_blocks_machines/certus_quartz_crystal)Certus Quartz Crystal$(/l)s, and fortune will increase this number.$(br2)There are 4 tiers of budding certus blocks: Flawless, Flawed, Chipped, and Damaged, and you initially find them in $(l:ae2_mechanics/meteorites)meteorites$(/l).
Every time a bud grows by another stage, the budding block has a chance to degrade

by one tier, eventually turning into a plain certus quartz block. They can be repaired (and new budding blocks created) by throwing the budding block (or a certus quartz block) in water with one or more $(l:items_blocks_machines/certus_quartz_crystal_charged)Charged Certus Quartz Crystal$(/l).

pages.title: Throw in Water
pages.text: Throw the items into water together.

Flawless budding certus blocks will not degrade and will generate certus infinitely. However they cannot be crafted or moved with a pickaxe, even with silk touch. (they $(o)can$() be moved with $(l:ae2_mechanics/spatial_io)spatial storage$(/l) though)$(br2)By themselves, certus quartz buds grow very slowly. Luckily the $(l:items_blocks_machines/growth_accelerator)Growth Accelerator$(/l) massively accelerates this process when placed adjacent to the budding block. You should build a few of these as

pages.text: If you don't have enough quartz to also make an $(l:items_blocks_machines/energy_acceptor)Energy Acceptor$(/l) or $(l:items_blocks_machines/vibration_chamber)Vibration Chamber$(/l),
